conversation.speaker: dialogue
conversation.text:
Police: Did you receive the admission notice? I heard you didn’t go to register.
Police: I came to investigate the situation. Times are not like before. Just consider it as me being nosy.
Police: The subdistrict office said they have already spoken with Xiyuan’s grandmother on the phone, but I still think it’s better to come and communicate face to face.
Police: Is Xiyuan doing well?
Respondent: Of course.
Respondent: Do you visit every household in person? That must be very hard.
Respondent: You’ll see in a moment. She’s very healthy now and is completely ready to attend school.
Respondent: After staying in the hospital for so long, it’s amazing that she’s still so lively and cheerful.
Respondent: Her personality might be inherited from her father. She already made people worry when she was still in my womb.
Respondent: Oh, I haven’t told you, right? Our Xiyuan was born prematurely at seven months.
Respondent: Every time the doctor saw me, he would scare me, saying she might have this or that problem, and handed me a stack of consent forms to sign.
Respondent: But I always believed that she would pull through and tightly grasp me with her little hands.
Respondent: If you’re worried that we’re abusing the child or something, that’s completely unnecessary.
Respondent: Although Xiyuan’s father and I are not living together now, her grandmother and I take good care of her.
Respondent: We will definitely attend the school opening ceremony.
Respondent: Thank you for caring about us so much.
Respondent: The meal seems to be ready. Would you like to eat before you leave?
